# sapjs

> sapjs is a reactive layer for hand-written HTML files. State, formulas and output are
> plain attributes, and the DOM is the only store: every change rebuilds the whole state
> tree by reading the live page, so there is no JavaScript state object that can drift.
> One script tag, no build step, no virtual DOM. Because the data lives in the markup,
> saving the file saves the app, rows and all.

This file is the complete reference for agents writing sapjs apps. It is condensed from
the source at https://github.com/panphora/sapjs and the human-readable site at
https://saphtml.com. Every attribute name, helper, format and error code below was read
out of the source. The npm package is `@panphora/sapjs`, the browser global is `Sap`, and
the license is MIT-0 (MIT No Attribution).

sapjs competes with Alpine plus a little hand-written JavaScript, not with React. It suits
trackers, calculators, forms with real validation, small CRUD apps and prototypes that fit
in one screen of readable HTML. It is a poor fit for large datasets, data behind
permissions, or an app that is mostly a window onto a server.

## Install

Classic script tag, auto-mounts every `[sap]` root on load:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@panphora/sapjs/dist/sap.min.js"></script>
```

The bundle is an IIFE, about 49 KB minified. Do not add `type="module"` to that tag. Pin a
version with `@panphora/sapjs@0.2.4` (or `@0.2`) in the URL. The same file is on unpkg at
`https://unpkg.com/@panphora/sapjs/dist/sap.min.js`, and the site serves it at
`https://saphtml.com/dist/sap.min.js`. Unminified: `dist/sap.js`.

As a module:

```bash
npm install @panphora/sapjs
```

```js
import Sap from "@panphora/sapjs";
```

The ES module entry is `src/sap.js` (untranspiled ES2022+, no dependencies). Importing it
has the same side effects as the script tag: it mounts every `[sap]` root on
`DOMContentLoaded` (or immediately if the document has already loaded) and assigns
`window.Sap`. sapjs needs a DOM, so it does nothing under SSR.

## Quick start

A complete file. Save it as `app.html` and open it. No server, no build.

```html
<!doctype html>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@panphora/sapjs/dist/sap.min.js"></script>

<main sap>
  <label>Quantity <input type="number" bind="qty" value="3"></label>
  <label>Unit price <input type="number" bind="price" value="10"></label>
  <output calc:total="state.qty * state.price" text:usd="state.total">$30</output>
</main>
```

Typing in either box recomputes `total` and repaints the `<output>` as `$30`. Pre-filling
the output with the value it will paint is deliberate: the file then renders correctly
before JavaScript runs, and sapjs reports `mount writes 0`, meaning it changed no bytes at
mount. Leave it empty and the app still works, but mount writes 1 and sapjs logs a `W30`
warning telling you to save once so the file settles.

## The pass: how everything works

One change causes one pass, and a pass is the entire engine:

1. Intake. Walk the app root top to bottom, reading every `state=` declaration, every
   `bind` control and every `items` list into fresh plain objects.
2. Compute. Run `calc:` expressions, deepest scope first, and in dependency order inside
   each scope, so a calc that reads another calc evaluates after it.
3. Paint. Evaluate `text`, `show`, `attr:`, `class:`, `css:`, then `effect=`, then
   `invalid=`. A paint writes only when the new value differs from what is already there.
4. Discard. The objects are thrown away. Nothing is retained between passes except the
   compiled-expression cache.

Because nothing is retained, a devtools edit, a console paste, a live-sync morph and a
keystroke are all the same thing: input to the next pass.

Passes are batched. A burst of writes coalesces into one pass on the next microtask, so
reading painted output on the line right after a write still sees the old DOM. Call
`Sap.refresh()` to force one synchronous pass and read the painted result immediately.

A pass suppresses its own writes, so a paint can never schedule another pass. If an app
does run away, a circuit breaker halts it after 50 passes in one macrotask and logs `E26`
naming the recent triggers.

## Roots

`sap` marks a mount root. Apps are isolated from each other: linting, the DOM walk, scope
resolution and scheduling all stop at the root. A page may hold any number of roots.

```html
<main sap>...</main>
<aside sap="sidebar">...</aside>
```

The root's `id`, or the value of `sap=` when there is no id, names the app in diagnostics.

`Sap.mount(rootOrSelector)` mounts a root added after load and returns its app record;
already-mounted roots are returned unchanged. `Sap.mount()` with no argument rescans the
document and returns the newly mounted records. A `[sap]` root injected into the page later
is picked up automatically by the mutation bridge.

## Declaring state

Three attributes put a field into the state tree.

```html
<main sap state="filter=all step:num=1 done:bool secret:transient">
```

`state=` is a space-separated list of declarations, each `name`, `name:type`,
`name=default` or `name:type=default`. Types are `string` (the default), `num` and `bool`.
A declared field's value lives in a same-named attribute on the declaring element, so
`state="filter=all"` pairs with `filter="all"`.

- Names must be valid identifiers. A hyphen halts the app with `E08`, because `due-date`
  parses as subtraction in an expression.
- HTML lowercases attribute names, so field names are effectively lowercase. Write
  `calc:linetotal`, not `calc:lineTotal`. The dependency scanner that orders calcs only
  matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` after `state.` or `item.`, so a camelCase name would also order
  wrongly.
- Declaring a reserved sapjs word halts with `E05`, a global HTML attribute name with
  `E06`, the same name twice in one scope with `E04`, and `state="open"` on a `<dialog>`
  with `E33` (use `showModal()` for a dialog; `state="open"` is fine on a `<details>`
  that also carries `scope=`, see below).

A declared field with no matching attribute reads its default and writes nothing. The one
exception: a field that a visibility verb (`show-when:` and family) reads is materialized
into its attribute at mount if missing, so the literal comparison has something to match.

`state=` is only read on a scope element: the app root, an element carrying `scope=`, an
`[item]` row, or a `[detail]` panel. On a plain element it is silently ignored, which is
the most common way a first sapjs app fails to work. Where it lands differs too: on a row
the fields belong to `item`, and a `[detail]` panel's declarations belong to the enclosing
scope so that the row's `set:` and the panel's key expression address one field.

```html
<div state="n:num=5"></div>              <!-- ignored: no scope here -->
<div scope="box" state="n:num=5"></div>  <!-- read, as state.box.n from the parent -->
```

When a declared field's name is a native boolean attribute and the element really has that
IDL property, sapjs reads it by presence rather than by value. That is what makes a native
`<details>` work as state, and it needs a `scope=` to be read at all:

```html
<details scope="sec" state="open" open>
  <summary>Section A <span text="state.open ? 'open' : 'collapsed'">open</span></summary>
  <p>The open attribute is real DOM state: it serializes and renders before JavaScript.</p>
</details>
```

`bind="field"` declares a field carried by a form control or a text leaf. `items="name"`
declares a field that is an array of rows. `scope="name"` opens a nested state object read
as `state.name` from the parent; scopes nest to any depth (`state.a.b.n`).

`sap-ignore` on any element makes it and its subtree invisible to sapjs: the pass never
walks into it, the linter skips it whole, and mutations inside it schedule nothing. This is
the escape hatch for third-party widgets and rich-text editors.

## bind: two-way, by control type

The control is the contract. There are no modifiers.

| Control | Value read and written |
|---|---|
| `input[type=text]`, `email`, `url`, `date`, `time`, `search`, `tel`, `password` | string |
| `input[type=number]`, `input[type=range]` | number |
| `input[type=checkbox]` | boolean |
| `input[type=radio]` (put `bind` on each radio in the `name` group) | the checked radio's value |
| `input[type=hidden]` | string |
| `textarea` | string |
| `select` | the selected option's value |
| `select[multiple]` | array of value strings |
| `[contenteditable]` or an empty text leaf such as `<span bind="x">` | `textContent` |

Number reads never produce `NaN`: an empty field reads `0`, and a value the browser flags
as bad input falls back to the `value` attribute or the last good number.

Mount errors on `bind`:

- `bind` on `input[type=file]` always halts (`E32`); files never serialize into an HTML file.
- `bind` on `input[type=password]` halts unless the input also carries `transient` (`E31`).
  A saved file must never carry a cleartext password.
- `bind` on an element that has child elements and is not `contenteditable` halts (`E20`),
  because the first write would wipe the subtree.
- `attr:value`, `attr:checked` or `attr:selected` on a bound control halts (`E30`); `bind`
  owns those attributes. An `effect=` that assigns `value` or `checked` on a bound control
  halts for the same reason.
- `text` or `text:FMT` on a form control halts (`E18`); paint into an `<output>` or `<span>`.
  `show=` on a control is allowed.

### step on a bound text input

A `step` attribute on a bound text-kind input (`type=text`, `tel` or `search`) makes
ArrowUp and ArrowDown adjust the value the way a native number input does, without the
spinner. Shift multiplies the step by 10, and `min` and `max` clamp the result. Native
`type=number` inputs are left alone.

```html
<input bind="amount" value="200" step="10" min="0" max="1000">
```

### default: the reset value

`default` on a bound control supplies the value `trigger-reset` and `$reset()` restore. Without
it a reset falls back to the control's `value` attribute, or `checked` for checkboxes and
radios. Attribute-carried state uses the default inside its own `state=` declaration instead.

```html
<main sap state="mode=compact">
  <input bind="name" value="Ada" default="Ada">
  <input type="checkbox" bind="updates" checked default="true">
  <button trigger-reset>Reset</button>
</main>
```

## calc: computed fields

```html
<dd calc:subtotal="sum(state.lines, 'linetotal')" text:usd2="state.subtotal"></dd>
<dd calc:total="state.subtotal + state.tax" text:usd2="state.total"></dd>
```

A `calc:` field belongs to the nearest owner: the row when the element is inside an
`[item]`, otherwise the nearest scope. Order is by dependency, not document position, so `total` waits for `subtotal` with no
help. Deeper scopes compute before shallower ones, so a row calc is ready when the parent
aggregates over it.

A cycle logs `E07` naming the chain, then falls back to source-order evaluation: the values
may be wrong, but the app keeps running. An expression that throws sets the field to
`undefined`, logs `E24`, and puts a `sap-error` attribute on the element.

Computed fields are read-only. Writing one from the scope that carries the `calc:`
attribute is rejected with `E16`. Writing one from further out is not caught, but it never
sticks either, because the next pass recomputes the field; all it leaves behind is a junk
declaration on the root.

## Paints

| Attribute | Writes |
|---|---|
| `text="expr"` | `textContent` |
| `text:FMT="expr"` | `textContent`, run through the named format |
| `show="expr"` | toggles the native `hidden` attribute (falsy hides) |
| `attr:NAME="expr"` | an attribute; native booleans toggle by presence |
| `class:NAME="expr"` | adds or removes one class |
| `css:NAME="expr"` | sets the `--NAME` custom property in the inline style |
| `effect="statement"` | runs a statement after paint, for side effects only |
| `invalid="expr"` | passes a truthy string to `setCustomValidity`, empty string clears it |

```html
<div css:fill="state.pct + '%'" class:hot="state.pct > 80"></div>
<button attr:disabled="state.pct >= 100" set:pct="100">Finish</button>
<p show="state.pct >= 100">Done</p>
<input type="number" bind="hi"
       invalid="state.hi < state.lo ? 'High must be at least Low' : ''">
```

Native boolean attributes recognised by `attr:`: `disabled`, `readonly`, `required`,
`checked`, `selected`, `multiple`, `open`, `inert`, `autofocus`, `novalidate`, `hidden`.
For visibility use `show=`, not `attr:hidden`, which warns with `W03`.

A paint writes only what changed, and a throwing paint writes nothing: the element keeps
its last good value, gets a `sap-error="E24"` attribute, and one attributed error is logged.

`effect=` is compiled as a statement and is for side effects only: touch `el`, set
`document.title`, drive a chart library. Assigning to `state.*` inside an effect does
nothing, because it mutates a per-pass object that is then discarded. Write state through
`onclick` and `Sap(this)` instead.

`invalid=` is the one expression that fails quietly. If it throws, the field is treated as
valid and nothing is logged, so guard those expressions against undefined or a bug there
silently disables the gate.

sapjs adopts three CSS rules at mount, through `adoptedStyleSheets` so they never serialize
into the saved file (engines without constructable stylesheets get a `<style id="sap-styles">`
node instead):

```css
[item][template] { display: none !important }
[hidden]         { display: none !important }
[sap-error]      { outline: 2px solid #e5484d; outline-offset: 1px }
```

The `[hidden]` rule matters: without it, any `display` rule of your own would beat the
browser's default styling of `hidden` and `show=` would appear to do nothing.

## Visibility: show versus show-when

Two families, and the shape tells you which engine runs.

| Attribute | Resolves | Works without sapjs |
|---|---|---|
| `show="expr"` | a JavaScript expression | no |
| `show-when:FIELD="a\|b"` | visible when the nearest self-or-ancestor `FIELD` attribute equals `a` or `b` | yes, through hyperclay's CSS floor |
| `hide-when:FIELD="a\|b"` | hidden when `FIELD` equals one of the values, shown otherwise, including when the attribute is absent | yes |
| `option:FIELD="a"` | alias of `show-when:` | yes |
| `option-not:FIELD="a"` | visible when `FIELD` is present and not equal to a listed value | yes |

The `show-when` family compares a plain attribute against literal values separated by `|`.
It never evaluates JavaScript. Writing an expression there (`show-when:tab="state.tab"`)
warns with `W04`; use `show=` for anything beyond literal equality.

```html
<main sap state="tab=overview">
  <button set:tab="'overview'">Overview</button>
  <button set:tab="'pricing'">Pricing</button>
  <section show-when:tab="overview">...</section>
  <section show-when:tab="pricing|faq">...</section>
</main>
```

Because `state="tab=overview"` materializes `tab="overview"` on the root, and `set:tab`
writes that same attribute, the two halves line up. When hyperclay's `optionVisibility` CSS
floor is loaded, sapjs stands down and lets CSS own visibility, so the two never fight and
the same markup works with either library alone.

With hyperclay or clayjs loaded, `<html>` carries `editmode="true|false"` and
`pageowner="true|false"`, reset to `false` before a save. So `show-when:editmode="true"` is
the way to show edit-only UI that is always hidden in the saved file, with no `state=` of
your own. Standalone, nothing stamps `editmode`, so that UI stays hidden.

## Actions as attributes

A click walks up from the target to the app root and runs the first element carrying an
action, so the innermost action wins.

| Attribute | Does |
|---|---|
| `set:field="expr"` | writes a field on click |
| `trigger-add="list"` | clones the list's `[item template]` and appends a row |
| `trigger-remove` | removes the nearest row |
| `trigger-reset` | resets the scope's controls and declared fields to their defaults |
| `move:up`, `move:down` | swaps a row with its neighbour |
| `move:to="list"` | moves a row into another list |
| `sort:FIELD` | stable sort of the list by that field, direction toggles on each click |
| `confirm="msg"` | gates any of the above behind a confirmation dialog |
| `detail="LIST by KEYEXPR"` | projects the selected row into a panel |

`sort:FIELD` takes an optional value naming the list (`sort:name="people"`); with no value
it uses the nearest `[items]` ancestor, then the first list in the scope. The direction is
stateless: sapjs sorts ascending, notices the order did not change, and reverses.

`confirm="msg"` evaluates its value as an expression when it parses as one, otherwise uses
it as a literal string. It calls the platform's themed dialog (`clay.confirm` or
`hyperclay.consent`) when one is present, and `window.confirm` otherwise.

`trigger-reset` and `$reset()` restore each bound control to its `default` attribute when
it has one, otherwise to its `value` attribute (checkboxes and radios to their `checked`
attribute), and each declared field to its `state=` default.

### trigger-add on a form

On a `<form>`, `trigger-add` fires on submit rather than click. It clones the template,
copies every bound control in the form into the new row's field of the same name, clears
the form, and refocuses the first field for rapid entry. Native `required` blocks empty
submits with no code.

```html
<main sap>
  <form trigger-add="todos">
    <input bind="title" placeholder="What needs doing?" required autofocus>
  </form>

  <ul items="todos">
    <li item template>
      <input type="checkbox" bind="done">
      <span bind="title" contenteditable="plaintext-only"></span>
      <button trigger-remove>x</button>
    </li>
  </ul>

  <output text="plural(count(state.todos, t => !t.done), 'task', 'tasks') + ' left'"></output>
</main>
```

That is a complete todo app with no JavaScript. The form's field is named `title`, the same
as the row's field, which is what lets the new row be composed from it.

## Actions in JavaScript: Sap(el)

`Sap(elOrSelector)` returns a live write-through proxy onto the scope or row that owns the
element. Reads come from the DOM, writes go through the one write path. It returns `null`
when the element is not inside a mounted app.

```html
<button onclick="['Buy milk','Walk dog'].forEach(t => Sap(this).$add('todos').title = t)">
  Add starter tasks
</button>
<button onclick="Sap(this).inbox.filter(m => m.picked).forEach(m => m.$remove())">
  Delete selected
</button>
```

Proxy members:

- `proxy.field` reads, `proxy.field = v` writes.
- `$el` the owning element, `$key` its id (stamped if missing), `$index` its position among
  its sibling rows, or `-1` outside a list.
- `$add(nameOrPath)` clones that list's template, appends it, and returns the new row's
  proxy.
- `$reset()` resets the scope to defaults and returns the proxy.
- `$remove()` removes the row. Throws on a stale handle to an already-removed row.
- `$move(listElementOrPath)` moves the row into another list.

List paths resolve nearest-scope-first: `"cards"` finds the nearest owned `items="cards"`,
and `"doing.cards"` finds `[scope="doing"] [items="cards"]`.

Writing a field that is not declared anywhere behaves in one of three ways:

- If the name is within edit distance 2 of a known field and at least 4 characters long,
  sapjs treats it as a typo and reports `E12` with a did-you-mean instead of creating it.
- If the name is a reserved sapjs word or a global HTML attribute name, it reports `E15`.
- Otherwise it is genuinely new, so sapjs appends a declaration to the app root's `state=`
  (inferring `num`, `bool` or string from the value) and sets the attribute. The DOM stays
  the truth.

Reserved sapjs words: `sap`, `scope`, `items`, `item`, `template`, `bind`, `calc`, `text`,
`show`, `attr`, `set`, `trigger`, `move`, `sort`, `detail`, `effect`, `invalid`, `confirm`,
`transient`, `default`, `persist`, `sortable`, `editmode`.

Global HTML names that cannot be fields: `title`, `style`, `hidden`, `lang`, `dir`,
`translate`, `class`, `id`, `nonce`, `autofocus`, `tabindex`, `contenteditable`,
`spellcheck`, `draggable`, `role`, `slot`, `part`, `name`, `value`, `type`, `itemscope`,
`itemtype`, `itemid`, `itemprop`, `itemref`.

## Expressions

Every expression compiles once against a frozen signature and is cached by source text:

```js
(state, item, el, root, fmt, num, sum, count, avg, min, max, plural, days)
```

- `state` is the nearest scope object, `item` the nearest row (`null` outside a list),
  `root` the app scope, `el` the element carrying the attribute.
- `fmt` is the format registry, so `fmt.usd2(state.total)` works inside any expression.
- Row metadata is on the row object: `item.$key`, `item.$index`, `item.$el`.
- Expressions are read-only. All writing happens through `Sap(el)` or the action attributes.

Helpers, all of which tolerate junk input rather than throwing:

- `num(v)` coerces anything to a number, never `NaN`. It strips `$`, `,`, `%` and
  whitespace first, so `"$1,200"` reads as `1200` and `"12%"` as `12`. Blank and unparsable
  values read as `0`.
- `sum(rows, key|fn)` adds `num()` of each row's key or callback result.
- `count(rows, pred?)` counts rows, or rows matching the predicate.
- `avg(rows, key|fn)` returns `0` for an empty list.
- `min(rows, key|fn)` and `max(rows, key|fn)` skip null and empty values, compare
  numerically when every value is numeric and as strings otherwise, and return `0` when
  nothing is left.
- `plural(n, singular, plural?)` returns `"3 tasks"`, defaulting the plural to `singular + "s"`.
- `days(a, b)` returns whole days from `a` to `b`, and `0` if either date is unparsable.

Because `num()` never yields `NaN`, a typo'd field name in an aggregate quietly sums to 0
rather than exploding. A numeric format applied to a non-finite value does still throw, as
`E22`, so bad numbers surface at the point where they would be shown.

### Formats

Built in: `usd`, `usd2`, `pct`, `pct1`, `int`, `num`, `num2`, `compact`, `date`, `clock`.

| Format | `text:FMT` of a sample value |
|---|---|
| `usd` | `1234.5` becomes `$1,235` |
| `usd2` | `1234.5` becomes `$1,234.50` |
| `pct` | `42.4` becomes `42%` |
| `pct1` | `42.44` becomes `42.4%` |
| `int` | `1234567` becomes `1,234,567` |
| `num` | locale-grouped number |
| `num2` | always two decimals |
| `compact` | `1234567` becomes `1.2M` |
| `date` | a date string becomes a US-locale date, or the raw string if unparsable |
| `clock` | milliseconds become `1:35.4` |

All the numeric formats throw `E22` on `NaN` or `Infinity` instead of painting "NaN".
Register your own, which is the library's only extension point:

```js
Sap.formats.eur = (n) => "EUR " + Number(n).toFixed(2);
Sap.config({ formats: { eur: (n) => "EUR " + Number(n).toFixed(2) } });
```

```html
<output text:eur="state.price"></output>
```

## Collections

`items="name"` on a container makes its `[item]` children the rows of `state.name`. Rows
must be direct children of the container. An `[item]` anywhere else halts with `E10`. The
one child carrying `[item template]` is the prototype cloned by `trigger-add` and `$add()`;
it is hidden by the runtime stylesheet and is never a row.

Each row with no id of its own is stamped with a generated one (`row-4`, `row-1a`), and that id
is the row's `$key`. Cloning a row assigns fresh ids throughout, so `$key` stays unique.

```html
<main sap>
  <ul items="lines">
    <li item template>
      <input type="number" bind="qty" value="1">
      <input type="number" bind="price" value="0">
      <output calc:linetotal="item.qty * item.price" text:usd2="item.linetotal"></output>
    </li>
  </ul>
  <output calc:total="sum(state.lines, 'linetotal')" text:usd2="state.total"></output>
</main>
```

Nesting works past one level. A row that declares `items="cards"` exposes them as
`item.cards`, and `Sap(this).$add('cards')` adds a card inside that row. Cloning the row
keeps its inner template.

```html
<main sap items="columns">
  <section item template>
    <input bind="title">
    <ul items="cards"><li item template bind="name"></li></ul>
    <button onclick="Sap(this).$add('cards')">Add card</button>
  </section>
</main>
```

Filter by hiding, never by removing, so aggregates still see every row:

```html
<input type="search" bind="q" transient>
<li item
    calc:match="state.q === '' || item.name.toLowerCase().includes(state.q.toLowerCase())"
    show="item.match">
```

### detail panels

`detail="LIST by KEYEXPR"` projects one row of a list into a panel. Edits inside the panel
are written through to the source row, and `Sap(this)` inside the panel resolves to that
row, so `$remove()` and `$move()` work there.

```html
<main sap state="selected">
  <ul items="contacts">
    <li item template set:selected="item.$key"><span bind="name"></span></li>
  </ul>

  <form detail="contacts by state.selected">
    <label>Name <input bind="name"></label>
    <label>Email <input type="email" bind="email"></label>
    <button onclick="Sap(this).$remove()">Delete</button>
  </form>
</main>
```

The panel sets `hidden` when nothing matches. It also hides silently when the `by` key
expression throws or the spec does not parse: no error, no beacon. If a panel never
appears, check that the key expression resolves to the selected row's `$key`. An `items=`
list inside a `detail=` panel is a mount error (`E17`); that is the one nesting limit.

## Persistence: what survives a save

sapjs state lives in the DOM, so the markup, the rows, the attributes and every
`textContent` are already in whatever HTML you save. There is one gap, and one attribute
that closes it.

Browser form state lives in JavaScript properties (`.value`, `.checked`, `.selected`), not
in attributes, and serialization only sees attributes. So when a user types into an input,
sapjs recomputes but does not touch the `value` attribute. A programmatic write does mirror:
`Sap(el).x = v`, `set:`, a reset, a form compose and a detail projection all write the live
property and then the serializable attribute.

Add `persist` to any control whose typed value must survive a save. sapjs honours it
itself, with no host platform involved, and it works with or without `bind`:

```html
<input bind="city" value="Lisbon" persist>
<textarea bind="notes" persist></textarea>
<select bind="plan" persist><option value="free">Free</option><option value="pro">Pro</option></select>
```

The rule of thumb: `bind` is reactivity, `persist` is durability. `persist` goes on the
control itself, never on a wrapper.

| Control | Does a typed value survive a plain save without `persist`? |
|---|---|
| `[contenteditable]` or bound text leaf | yes, it is `textContent` |
| text or number input | no |
| checkbox or radio | no |
| select or select-multiple | no |
| textarea | no |

What the mirror writes per control: `checked` for checkboxes and radios, `value` for other
inputs, `selected` on each option for selects, and a cursor-safe `data-value` attribute for
textareas (writing a focused textarea's `textContent` would destroy the caret). At mount,
any `textarea[data-value]` is rehydrated back into the live value, so the value round-trips
across a reload even without a save step. A platform save resolves `data-value` into real
`textContent` through `Sap.finalizeControlForSave`.

### transient: the opposite of persist

`transient` keeps a value out of the saved file. It is a bare attribute on a control, or a
`:transient` suffix in a declaration:

```html
<input type="search" bind="q" transient>
<input type="password" bind="pw" transient>
<main sap state="draft:transient">
```

A transient control's `value`, `checked` and `data-value` attributes are stripped on every
pass, including stale ones left over from an earlier save, and the live property carries the
value instead. A transient declared field lives on a runtime-only property, so its
attribute never appears at all while the `state=` declaration stays.

`transient` and `persist` on one control halts the app with `E34`: their intents are
opposite and `persist` would win, leaking exactly what `transient` promised to drop.

## What triggers a pass

sapjs installs one delegated listener set on `document`, plus a mutation observer.

- `input` and `change` on any control inside a root.
- `click` on an element carrying an action attribute.
- `submit` on a `<form trigger-add>`, and native `reset` on any form.
- `toggle` on `<details>`, in the capture phase, so a `<details scope="sec" state="open">`
  recomputes when the user opens or closes it.
- `keydown` for ArrowUp and ArrowDown on a bound text input carrying `step`.
- `clay:sorted`, the event a hyperclay or clayjs `sortable` drag dispatches after a reorder.
- Any DOM mutation. Standalone this is a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` watching
  childList, subtree, attributes and characterData. When the platform's mutation hub is
  present sapjs rides that instead, and a native observer hands over to a hub that arrives
  late. Either way, edits made by devtools, a console paste, another library or a live-sync
  morph all trigger a pass, and mutations inside `[sap-ignore]` or `[template]` are ignored.

Every write a pass makes is suppressed at the observer, so paints never feed back.

Because the bridge is a mutation observer, **anything that changes the DOM recomputes for
free**, including changes made by code that has never heard of sapjs:

```js
document.querySelector("main[sap]").setAttribute("tax", "0.08");
document.querySelector("[contenteditable][bind=title]").textContent = "Changed outside sapjs";
```

**But assigning a form control's property is not a DOM mutation and fires no event, so it
triggers nothing:**

```js
document.querySelector("[bind=title]").value = "Changed";   // sapjs never notices
```

After a direct property assignment, either dispatch an `input` or `change` event, write through
`Sap(el)` instead, or call `Sap.refresh()`. This is the usual reason a scripted change appears
in the box but never reaches the state tree.

## JavaScript API

| Call | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Sap(elOrSelector)` | live write-through proxy onto the owning scope or row, or `null` |
| `Sap.mount(rootOrSelector)` | mount one root and return its record; no argument rescans the document |
| `Sap.refresh()` | one synchronous pass over every connected app |
| `Sap.batch(label, fn)` | run `fn`, then commit it as one labelled undo entry when the platform's undo is present |
| `Sap.formats` | the format registry, extend it with `Sap.formats.name = fn` |
| `Sap.config({ formats })` | same, as a config object; returns `Sap` |
| `Sap.status()` | machine-readable twin of the mount line |
| `Sap.report()` | every error and warning as JSON |
| `Sap.why(el, field?)` | log how a field resolves: attributes, scope snapshot, serialization note |
| `Sap.debug(true)` | log a header for every pass with the trigger and the write count |
| `Sap.doctor()` | full-page audit, returns an array of findings |
| `Sap.version` | the engine version string |
| `Sap.serializeControlToAttributes(el)` | mirror one control's live state into attributes, live and cursor-safe |
| `Sap.finalizeControlForSave(target, source?)` | mirror for a save, resolving a textarea's `data-value` into `textContent` |
| `Sap.rehydrateControlFromAttributes(el)` | load-time inverse for a textarea carrying `data-value` |

`Sap.batch(label, fn)` throws if `fn` is not a function, and throws if `fn` returns a
promise; the batch must be synchronous.

```js
Sap.batch("clear completed", () => {
  Sap("#todos").todos.filter(t => t.done).forEach(t => t.$remove());
});
```

Writing then reading needs a refresh, because passes are batched:

```js
Sap(el).qty = 12;
Sap.refresh();
el.querySelector("output").textContent; // now current
```

The entry module also exposes `Sap._registry` (the root-to-record `Map`), `Sap._reset()`, and a
named `runtime` export carrying `apps()`, `appFor(el)`, `isRegistered(el)`,
`pruneDisconnected()`, `schedule(app, trigger)`, `runNow(app, trigger)`, `moveInto()`,
`placeBefore()` and `remountIfPresent()`. The site and the test suite use these. **They are
internal surfaces, not application API**, and nothing outside the repository should depend on
them.

## The console contract

Each app logs one machine-readable line when it mounts:

```
sap ✓ main[sap] · fields 12 · calcs 4 · paints 18 · actions 6 · lists 2 · rows 7 · warnings 0 · mount writes 0 · 1.8ms
```

A failing app logs `sap ✗ main[sap] · errors 1 · warnings 0 · 0.4ms` through `console.error`
instead. `mount writes 0` is the zero-byte-mount guarantee: sapjs read the file and changed
nothing in it.

`Sap.status()` returns `{ ok, apps: [...] }`, where each app carries `root`, `fields`,
`calcs`, `paints`, `actions`, `lists`, `rows`, `warnings`, `errors`, `mountWrites`, `ms`,
`passes`, `lastPass` and `ok`.

`Sap.report()` returns `{ ok, errors, warnings, counts }`. Each record is
`{ code, slug, el, attr, expr, key, problem, didYouMean, fix, phase }`, where `el` is a
short CSS path such as `main[sap] > p > output`.

`Sap.doctor()` re-lints, then runs a dry pass and reports what a settled page should not
have: writes on a quiet page (`W30`), fields declared but read nowhere (`I33`), duplicate
ids (`W32`), expressions over 120 characters (`I33`), and paints showing more than four
decimals (`I33`). Doctor findings are advisory, not blocking.

Errors print with the element path, the authored attribute and source, and a fix:

```
sap ✗ E12 unknown-state-key
  at main[sap] > p > output
  problem: unknown state key "totl"
  did you mean: total
```

For an agent, the definition of done for a sapjs file is three checks: no `sap ✗` line in
the console, `Sap.status().ok === true`, and no elements matching `[sap-error]`.

### Error codes

Codes that halt are structural contradictions found by the mount linter. A halt skips the
mount pass entirely, so the app paints nothing on load, the file's bytes are exactly as they
were saved, and the root carries `sap-error="CODE"`. It is not a runtime guard: the
delegated listeners are shared across the page, so a later click on an action inside a
halted app can still write and repaint. Treat a halt as a build error to fix. Every other
code degrades per element, and the rest of the app keeps running.

| Code | Meaning | Halts at mount |
|---|---|---|
| `E01` | foreign-dialect attribute (`x-text`, `v-if`, `@click`, `:class`), teaches the sapjs spelling | yes |
| `E02` | moustaches in text content, which is not a sapjs feature | yes |
| `E04` | the same field declared twice in one scope | yes |
| `E05` | a reserved sapjs word used as a field name | yes |
| `E06` | a global HTML attribute name used as a field name | yes |
| `E07` | `calc:` cycle, names the chain, then falls back to source order | no |
| `E08` | expression does not parse, or a field name contains a hyphen | yes |
| `E10` | an `[item]` that is not a direct child of an `[items]` list | yes |
| `E12` | write to an unknown state key that looks like a typo, with a did-you-mean | no |
| `E15` | write to an undeclared reserved or global name | no |
| `E16` | write to a `calc:` field | no |
| `E17` | an action target that cannot be resolved, or `items` inside `detail`, or `trigger-add` at a list with no template | yes for the structural cases |
| `E18` | `text` or `text:FMT` on a form control | yes |
| `E20` | `bind` on a container element that is not contenteditable | yes |
| `E22` | a numeric format received `NaN` or `Infinity` | no |
| `E24` | an expression threw during a pass, last good value preserved | no |
| `E26` | the recompute circuit breaker tripped after 50 passes in one macrotask | halts at runtime |
| `E30` | `attr:value`, `attr:checked`, `attr:selected` or an `effect` write on a bound control | yes |
| `E31` | `bind` on a password input without `transient` | yes |
| `E32` | `bind` on a file input | yes |
| `E33` | `state="open"` on a `<dialog>` | yes |
| `E34` | `transient` and `persist` on one control | yes |
| `W03` | an unknown `prefix:` attribute, or a bare attribute close to a real one, with a did-you-mean | no |
| `W04` | a JavaScript expression given to `show-when:` or its family | no |
| `W30` | the app painted at mount, so the saved file was out of sync with its own state | no |

## Hyperclay and clayjs integration

sapjs runs standalone in any HTML file and needs no platform. When one of the malleable-HTML
clients is loaded (`window.hyperclay` from hyperclayjs, or `window.clay` from clayjs) sapjs
detects each capability independently and uses it:

- Live-sync. `hyperclay:livesync-applied` or `clay:sync-applied` triggers a synchronous
  re-derive, so a morph from another tab repaints immediately. If the morph replaced the
  `[sap]` element itself, sapjs drops the dead record and remounts.
- Mutations. `hyperclay.Mutation` or `clay.Mutation` replaces the native observer, so sapjs
  inherits the platform's pause windows and its own writes stay off autosave and undo.
- Undo. sapjs subscribes to the undo plugin's `undo` and `redo` events and re-derives after
  each replay, because replaying an attribute fires no event. `Sap.batch(label, fn)` labels a
  bulk mutation as one undo entry.
- Dialogs. `confirm=` uses `clay.confirm` or `hyperclay.consent` when present, with a guard
  so a second click cannot open a second dialog, and `window.confirm` otherwise.
- Regions. Inside a `no-save` or `freeze` region the persist mirror is skipped, because the
  platform strips those bytes anyway. The control stays fully live and reactive.
- Sorting. A `sortable` drag dispatches `clay:sorted` and sapjs re-derives both lists it
  touched.
- Visibility. When `optionVisibility` has started, sapjs stops setting `hidden` for
  `show-when` and lets the CSS floor own it.

Region and platform attributes the linter tolerates inside a root without warning:
`no-save`, `no-watch`, `no-undo`, `no-trigger-autosave`, `freeze`, `mutations-ignore`,
`save-remove`, `save-ignore`, `save-freeze`, `sortable`, and the whole `editmode:` family.

None of this needs configuration, and the same file works offline and online.

## Rich text

sapjs state is plaintext. A `bind` reads and writes `textContent`, never inner HTML, so
every value is a scalar that round-trips as text. Pasting formatted content into a bound
contenteditable flattens it to a string on read.

To embed a real editor, put `sap-ignore` on its mount. The pass never descends into it, the
linter skips it whole, so a third-party editor's own attributes never trip `E01`, and its
markup round-trips because the live DOM is saved as-is. sapjs can then own the block list
(`items`, `trigger-add`, `move:`, `trigger-remove`) while each block body stays rich.

```html
<li item template>
  <input bind="label">
  <div sap-ignore no-undo contenteditable="true">Rich <b>body</b> here.</div>
</li>
```

Practical notes: `sap-ignore` stops the DOM walk but not event delegation, so call
`stopPropagation()` on the editor's own `input` and `change` events to avoid needless
passes. Put `no-undo` on the mount so its keystrokes do not flood the undo stack, and avoid
`no-watch`, which turns autosave off too. sapjs cannot read the prose, so to compute over it
mirror a derived plaintext value into a normal field.

## Limits and non-goals

- Expressions compile with `new Function`, so a Content Security Policy without
  `'unsafe-eval'` breaks every expression in the page. There is no precompiled mode.
- The vocabulary is frozen. There are no custom directives and no plugin system, precisely
  so that an unknown attribute is always a typo and the did-you-mean guarantee holds. The
  one extension point is a custom text format.
- No moustache interpolation, and no `x-` or `v-` dialect. Both halt with a message naming
  the sapjs spelling.
- Field names must be lowercase identifiers with no hyphens.
- Expressions are read-only. Writing state inside `effect=` silently does nothing.
- Reading painted output on the line after a write sees the old DOM unless you call
  `Sap.refresh()`.
- `Sap.batch` must be synchronous.
- Rows are DOM elements, so a very large list is a very large document. There is no
  virtualization and no diffing beyond write-if-changed.
- An `items=` list inside a `detail=` panel is a mount error.
- State is plaintext scalars, arrays of rows and nested scope objects. Rich text, files and
  binary data live outside sapjs state.
- Nothing here is private. The data is in the markup, so a file that must hide data from
  the person holding it is the wrong shape for sapjs, and the library says so rather than
  pretending otherwise.
- The compiled-expression cache clears wholesale past 512 entries, and the circuit breaker
  halts an app after 50 passes in one macrotask.
- sapjs requires a DOM. There is no server-side rendering path.
